definition: An attention pattern where each token only attends to a fixed-size local window of nearby tokens, rather than the entire sequence.
details: Sliding window attention reduces the quadratic computational cost of full self-attention, trading some long-range direct interaction for substantial efficiency gains, often combined with other mechanisms to preserve some long-range information flow.

explainer.lead: Sliding window attention is an attention pattern where each token attends only to a fixed-size local window of nearby tokens rather than the entire sequence. It matters because it reduces the quadratic computational cost of full self-attention while trading away some long-range direct interaction.

tiers.eli5: Instead of every word in a sentence looking at every other word, each word only looks at its close neighbours. That's much cheaper, though distant words no longer see each other directly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use local windows to cut the cost of self-attention on long sequences, often combining them with other mechanisms to preserve some long-range information flow. A pitfall is assuming the window alone captures long-range dependencies, which it does not.
tiers.paperLevel: Each token attends to a fixed-size local window of nearby tokens instead of the full sequence, reducing the quadratic cost of full self-attention; some long-range direct interaction is lost and is often recovered via other mechanisms.

explainer.example: In a long document, a token attends only to the fixed number of tokens around it, and other mechanisms carry information between distant parts of the text.
